sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r5/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx — 'Quality Checks'!A16:D16 and 'Internal Quality Checks'!A16:D16 (row 15, C - environment/; no additional row-specific annotation beyond column D)
Own runtime: docker build of frozen task/environment (tag qc-r5-row15-kittle-agent:tmp, removed afterwards) + --network none container checks
evidence: Frozen environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (diff empty): FROM node:22-bookworm-slim (template-controlled pinned base, no --platform), NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules, npm install -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (exactly the two non-builtin requires in solution/app/server.js lines 10-11 and package.json), COPY instructions/ /instructions/ and COPY assets/ /assets/, chmod -R a+rX on both, /app created, git-initialised with only .gitkeep committed; no COPY of solution/ or tests/. I built the frozen environment context myself and ran it with --network none: npm ls -g shows express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1; require('express') and an in-memory better-sqlite3 query succeed offline; /assets/seed_data.json (sha b256f85e..., identical to solution/app/seed copy) and the three /instructions files are readable by user nobody; /app contains only .git and .gitkeep with one commit and clean status. Running the frozen solve.sh in that offline image and starting node /app/server.js as nobody under env -i with only PATH/NODE_PATH/HOME/PORT/DB_PATH (cwd /tmp) returned GET /api/health 200, so no run-time install is needed. integration.md line 3 publicly states Express and better-sqlite3 are preinstalled via NODE_PATH, matching the image. Adversarial: an app needing an extra npm package would have to vendor it in /app (agent network is public); that is a builder choice, not an image defect, and a node-builtins-only app also runs. Residual non-blocking note: the base is a major-version tag, not a digest, but that is template-controlled and must be preserved. Raw-evidence-index golden run used a different image (cw-editor-agent-r3, other task's assets), so I relied on my own build rather than that record.
